title: Converting white to okhsv produces NaN saturation
body:
### Tested versions

This is a bug in third party code that has not changed since it was added to Godot in 2022. It does not appear to be causing any problems in Godot currently, but it'd be nice to not divide by zero.

### System information

Godot v4.5.dev (32eafc18b) - Debian GNU/Linux trixie/sid trixie on Wayland - X11 display driver, Single-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (RPL-P) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1360P (16 threads)

### Issue description

`ok_color::srgb_to_okhsl({1, 1, 1})` produces hue = 0.25, saturation = NaN, luminance = 1.0.

In the UI, the NaN appears to just get coerced to zero:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b46fd670-d7aa-4376-b9bd-5293169fc61c)

I discovered this while trying to track down the root cause of some NaNs in my own code.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add `feenableexcept(FE_INVALID | FE_OVERFLOW);` to some part of Godot's startup code to enable floating point exceptions.
2. Run the Godot editor.
3. Godot will crash with this stack trace:
